newsitem.title: FRANCE: Dijon airport candidate for KLM cargo hub.
newsitem.headline: Dijon airport candidate for KLM cargo hub.

text.p: Dijon airport, in eastern France, said it was of one several sites being considered by KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV for a freighter sub-hub in eastern France.

"We have been in discussions with KLM over the past 18 months on the subject of all-cargo flights and expect them to come back to us with their decision, probably by the middle of next month," an official from Dijon's Chamber of Commerce, which runs the airport, told Reuters.
"We have a runway of 2,600 metres able to handle several types of freighter aircraft, although not a plane the size of Boeing 747 freighter," he said.
There are adequate warehousing facilities available for a rapid start-up of operations should KLM decide to go-ahead as well as excellent road and rail communications close to the airport, he added.
Dijon is around 300 kilometres south-east of Paris and some 200 kilometres north of Lyon and is already used for both civilian and military air transport.
French airline, Regional Airlines, operates a twice-daily passenger service between Dijon and Clermont-Ferrand.
The Chamber of Commerce official said KLM was also looking at Lyon-Satolas, Basle-Mulhouse and Strasbourg airports as possible sites for the freighter sub-hub.

In an interview with Reuters this week, KLM Cargo's Paris-based operations manager, Southern Europe, Simon Groenenboom, said KLM planned to set-up a cargo sub-hub serving France, Switzerland, Germany, northern Italy and Luxembourg, offering direct freighter connections to the Far East and the U.S.,
"This would take the pressure off our Schiphol hub while at the same time realising important economies of scale and providing greater proximity in terms of customer service.
"The sub-hub could begin first-phase operations by 1999 with a full-term objective being an annual throughput of traffic between 30,000-50,000 tonnes, Groenenboom said.
He declined however to comment on the specific sites under consideration. -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
